Hooks

Run shell commands automatically when Claude edits files, finishes tasks, or needs input. Deterministic automation.

What Are Hooks?

Hooks are shell commands that run at specific points in Claude's lifecycle. Unlike CLAUDE.md instructions (which Claude may or may not follow), hooks are deterministic — they always run.

CLAUDE.md instructions
Advisory

Claude tries to follow them. May be inconsistent.

Hooks
Deterministic

Always executes. Perfect for formatting, logging, blocking.

Set up hooks with /hooks in the CLI, or edit settings.json directly.

Hook Lifecycle Events

EventWhen it fires
SessionStartWhen a session begins or resumes
UserPromptSubmitWhen you submit a prompt, before Claude processes it
PreToolUseBefore a tool call executes — can block it
PostToolUseAfter a tool call succeeds
NotificationWhen Claude sends a notification (idle, needs input, etc.)
StopWhen Claude finishes responding
PreCompactBefore context compaction
SubagentStart / StopWhen a subagent spawns or finishes
ConfigChangeWhen a settings or skills file changes
WorktreeCreate / RemoveWhen worktrees are created or cleaned up

Your First Hook: Desktop Notifications

Get notified when Claude finishes or needs your input. Run /hooks → select Notification:

~/.claude/settings.jsonjson
{
  "hooks": {
    "Notification": [
      {
        "matcher": "",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "osascript -e 'display notification \"Claude needs your attention\" with title \"Claude Code\"'"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
macOS
osascript -e 'display notification "Claude" with title "Claude Code"'
Linux
notify-send 'Claude Code' 'Claude needs your attention'
Windows
powershell.exe -Command "[Windows.Forms.MessageBox]::Show('Claude needs your attention')"

Auto-Format Code After Edits

Run Prettier on every file Claude edits — automatically, every time:

.claude/settings.jsonjson
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "jq -r '.tool_input.file_path' | xargs npx prettier --write"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
Install jq for JSON parsing: brew install jq (macOS) or apt-get install jq (Linux).

Block Edits to Protected Files

Prevent Claude from modifying sensitive files like .env or package-lock.json:

.claude/hooks/protect-files.shbash
"color:#586e75">#!/bin/bash
INPUT=$("color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">cat)
FILE_PATH=$("color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.file_path // empty')

PROTECTED=(".env" "package-lock.json" ".">git/")

for pattern in "${PROTECTED[@]}"; do
  if [[ "$FILE_PATH" == *"$pattern"* ]]; then
    "color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">echo "Blocked: $FILE_PATH matches protected pattern '$pattern'" >&2
    exit 2   "color:#586e75"># exit 2 = block the action
  fi
done

exit 0  "color:#586e75"># exit 0 = allow
.claude/settings.jsonjson
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": ".claude/hooks/protect-files.sh" }]
      }
    ]
  }
}
Exit code 2 blocks the action. Claude receives anything you write to stderr as feedback so it can adjust. Exit code 0 allows. Any other exit code allows but logs the error.

Re-inject Context After Compaction

When Claude compacts, it can lose important context. Use a SessionStart hook with compact matcher to re-inject it:

.claude/settings.jsonjson
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "matcher": "compact",
        "hooks": [{
          "type": "command",
          "command": "echo 'Reminder: use pnpm (not npm). Run pnpm test before committing. Current sprint: auth refactor.'"
        }]
      }
    ]
  }
}

Matchers

Matchers filter when a hook fires — they're regex patterns:

Edit|Write→ Only on file-editing tools
Bash→ Only on shell commands
mcp__github__.*→ Any GitHub MCP tool
compact→ Only on compact SessionStart
""→ Every occurrence (no filter)
permission_prompt→ Only permission prompts in Notification

Prompt-Based Hooks

For decisions that need judgment, use type: "prompt" — Claude evaluates the condition:

json
{
  "hooks": {
    "Stop": [{
      "hooks": [{
        "type": "prompt",
        "prompt": "Check if all requested tasks are complete. If not, respond with {"ok": false, "reason": "what remains"}."
      }]
    }]
  }
}

If the model returns {"ok": false}, Claude keeps working using the reason as its next instruction. Perfect for quality gates.
